info.title: ai-sdlc gate
info.description: The deterministic half of ai-sdlc, which holds an AI coding agent, and the people directing it, to what was written down. Every change is planned before any code exists, challenged by a reader that never saw it written, approved by a person against the exact text, and proved from recorded evidence, against rules and decisions that live in the repository and carry from one cycle to the next. This is the `sdlc` command every host hook and pipeline step calls: it decides everything a program can, including the pull-request check that refuses a change whose chain is incomplete, unapproved or hash-mismatched. The stages need language and ship separately as the plugin.

commands.name: admit
commands.description:
In a sandbox: print the one git command that takes its
approved cycles' folders, and the successors it wrote, onto
cycle/<id>/plan for one or slices/sandbox-<id>/plan for
several, from the integration branch, in a worktree beside
the sandbox. What the gate does not let through stays. Refuses
outside a sandbox, with nothing approved, over uncommitted
changes in an approved cycle, and a plan that needs a file
only a sibling's plan creates. Abandoned cycles go with it as
records. 'sdlc build <id>' runs it, and /sdlc:pr --plan
runs it.

commands.name: areas
commands.description:
Each area areas.md defines: the files it covers today, the
rules and decisions carrying it, and entries naming an area
nobody defined. Exits 1 when an area covers no file, which
stops a round until it is fixed.

commands.name: backlog
commands.description:
Every successor and every parked cycle, in the waves they come
ready in -- ready now, then after one more merge, and so on
-- each with how to start it, and apart from them the stuck
and the unresolved. A view; it writes nothing (D-145).

commands.name: branch
commands.description:
Print the one git command that puts the working copy on the
branch a kind of work happens on -- plan, build,
build-unattended or forward -- creating it from the right
base: the integration branch once the plan is admitted to
it, before that the plan's own branch or the admission
branch carrying it. A plan only in a sandbox is refused
until 'sdlc admit' takes it out. 'sandbox' opens a
worktree on sandbox/<id> beside the repository, where every
cycle the work turns into is planned. 'plan --worktree'
opens the one cycle in a folder of its own. 'plan' without a
worktree refuses uncommitted work, which the switch would
carry, and a local plan branch whose ledger lacks the
approval the integration branch holds (D-123).

commands.name: branch-policy
commands.description:
Print the commands that set the default branch policy on
this solution's platform: pull requests only, nobody
bypassing, the pipeline required, squash into the
integration branch and merge commits into the default
branch. Applies nothing; run them as an administrator.
--approvals <n> asks every pull request for n approvals;
--owner <who>[,<who>] names who must give one, as a
CODEOWNERS line on GitHub and a required reviewer on
Azure DevOps; --self-approve lets an author's own vote
count on Azure DevOps, and on GitHub, which never counts
it, needs a team: --self-approve <team> lets that team
bypass the rules on a pull request.

commands.name: build
commands.description:
Build it (D-178, D-184, D-187): commits the approval a person
placed in the sandbox if it is uncommitted, admits the plan
when it is only in a sandbox, opens the build's worktree beside
the repository, starts the build's own process there running
/sdlc:build <id> --unattended -- headless, its tools named,
never with permission checks off, never marked as a reader --
waits, and prints the report. Exits 0 on a pass, 1 on blocked
or escalated. With no id, every queued cycle in one process
started from here, each in a worktree of its own; a plan only
in a sandbox is queued only when named. Refuses when the
build's process cannot start, or ends without a report. The
one stage this binary runs rather than names a skill for.

commands.name: claude
commands.description:
Start Claude Code with the skills this release carries, which
in a solution that pins a release are that release's. Every
argument after 'claude' is Claude Code's, passed unchanged.

commands.name: constraints
commands.description:
An empty entry at the next free LOC_ id, for a rule a person
has in mind. Writes nothing; takes no wording.

commands.name: show

commands.name: constraints
commands.description:
An empty entry at the next free LOC_ id, for a rule a person
has in mind. Writes nothing; takes no wording.

commands.name: cycles
commands.description:
What a build would take now -- approved, no verify, not
abandoned -- in the order to build it: the cycle the most
successors wait on first, then oldest. And every cycle held
back, with why: a cycle/<id>/... branch on the remote, or an
approval the gate no longer accepts. Deleting the branch
re-queues it. With an id, that cycle alone, and exits 1 with
why when it is not queued.

commands.name: decisions
commands.description:
The choices this solution has already settled, so a cycle reads
what was argued rather than arguing it again. CON_27 asks a cycle
departing from one to declare it where it arises. Names
the entries over the word budget, for a harvest to reword.

commands.name: show
commands.description:
One decision in full, standing or superseded: what a reader
handed only its headline asks for.

commands.name: deviations
commands.description:
Where the build bent the approved documents, and the choices
it made that they left open: each entry in deviations.md,
whether it is in force or was changed at the person's request,
and anything wrong with it. Exits 1 while a deviation misquotes
the approved text, takes a claimed file or narrows a criterion.

commands.name: discard
commands.description:
In a sandbox: what throwing it away would lose. Each cycle
is empty, can go, is worth recording -- it fixed a decision,
or its readers raised something -- or is recorded already.
Prints the removal for a person to run once nothing worth
recording is unrecorded, and exits 1 until then. Deletes
nothing.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description:
Check this installation and this repository: the rules, git,
how many decisions every reader is handed,
adoption, which release wrote adoption's files against this
binary, line endings, every host's hook config, and the
pipeline that is the guarantee, and asks the platform
through az or gh whether branch policy requires it.
Reports and never repairs. Exits 1 if anything is wrong, a
policy that does not require the check included. What it
cannot see -- whether a host loaded the skills, or the
policy when the CLI is not signed in -- is marked
'elsewhere' and names who to ask. Before the first
cycle it ends with what a person still has to place, and the
one command that is next.

commands.name: abandon
commands.description: Print the record that stops a cycle, for a person to place.

commands.name: approval
commands.description:
Write the gate decision beside the ledger, for a person to
rename onto it. Writes no approval.

commands.name: harvest
commands.description:
Write drafts of constraints.md, decisions.md, techstack.md and
areas.md from the proposals marked [x] in a harvest proposal
file: each a copy of the file as it stands with only those
lines applied, refused if any rule, decision or stack row
would go missing. An area may be renamed, merged or removed.

commands.name: solution
commands.description:
Write the whole solution.md beside itself, for a person
to rename onto it. Carries every key through as
recorded and the prose through unchanged, so the rename
cannot reclassify the solution or cost anybody what they
wrote. --approval, --coverage-floor and --standard each
change their one key when asked, and say so.

commands.name: techstack
commands.description:
Write the declared stack beside itself, for an edit a person
renames into place: a copy of it, or the framework's default
where there is none yet, with every stack rule listed and on.
The default also lists the five .NET build settings files, one
row each: on where the repository held no code, off where it
did. A row not true here says 'none' rather than being
deleted. On a copy, names what this release ships that the
stack never mentions, and adds none of it. Also reports the
options menu: every concern the shipped profiles know about,
what each declares, every stack rule, and what each build
settings file does and costs. The menu is never renamed into
place.

commands.name: Environment
commands.description:
SDLC_DEV_BUILD           A directory holding a build of sdlc nobody published. Every
command is handed to it instead of the pinned release, it
calls itself <release>-local, and no cycle it judged opens a
pull request. For testing a change to the framework.

commands.name: evidence
commands.description:
Record what a build produced: its base commit, the commit it is
at, the diff between them, a normalised test summary and the
coverage. Verify reads only this. The summary records the
platform the tests ran on. Refuses code outside .sdlc/ that is
not committed; the diff is rebuilt from the two commits and
never committed (D-124). Retires a blocked verify.md, and
refuses while any other verdict stands (D-161) -- unless
--retire-pass, when a person asked for a change to a cycle
that passed (D-185).

commands.name: check
commands.description:
List what verify.md cites in backticks that none of the
recorded evidence holds, and tests it says passed that did not.
Reports only; always exits 0.

commands.name: factory
commands.description:
Write the factory's pipeline for the recorded platform: a run
a person starts, never a schedule, of /sdlc:build
--unattended against the integration branch -- every queued
cycle, or the one named as its input -- one run at a time,
six hours at most, proving the hooks refuse before it builds,
and publishing the sitrep. It never merges. Refuses on a
local solution.

commands.name: findings
commands.description:
What the interrogations said, per artifact, each finding at the
disposition that stands.

commands.name: gate
commands.description: Say whether a cycle's build may run. Exits 1 if not.

commands.name: harvest
commands.description:
One aspect -- constraints, decisions, suggestions, stack or
areas -- for the completed cycles that have not answered it,
ending with the proposal file a person marks for 'draft
harvest'. Proposes; writes nothing that binds. --cycles reads
those cycles alone and leaves the rest for a later sitting;
the rule counts stay the whole completed record's. So:
harvest constraints, harvest decisions, harvest suggestions,
harvest stack, harvest areas.
harvest record <aspect> <file>
Once the aspect's draft is renamed into place: record in
.sdlc/harvested.json that the cycles the file's '## Cycles'
names have answered it, with the concerns under '## Watch' and
'## Ignored' tallied and the suggestions under '## Declined'
kept. Closes nothing. Refuses while the draft is still beside
its file.

commands.name: close
commands.description:
Close every completed cycle whose five aspects have all been
answered: record what later harvests need, and on a new
harvest/<date> branch commit the removal of their folders with
the ledger and the records a person placed. Pushes nothing.
Refuses, naming what each cycle still needs, while nothing can
close; while a draft is still beside its file; and anywhere
but the integration branch.
harvest read --dir <directory> [--aspect <aspect>] [--cycles <ids>]
Write one prompt per completed cycle and document with findings
in the aspect's sitting, constraints unless given, each that
document's findings and the question that groups them, and
start one fresh reader for each, its answer written beside its
prompt (D-183).
harvest review <aspect> --dir <directory> [--proposals <file>]
Write and start the two readers that review one aspect's
sitting: one handed the marked proposal file, the aspect's
draft and solution.md; one handed the aspect's report and the
proposal file. The newest of each in .sdlc/reports unless
--proposals names the file.

commands.name: help
commands.description: This text. So does --help after any command.

commands.name: hook
commands.description:
Judge a tool call, or a turn that is ending, or say as a session
starts that its skills are another release. Reads the host's
payload on stdin and writes its decision on stdout.
Hosts: claude, copilot, antigravity.

commands.name: init
commands.description:
Adopt the framework into this repository. Run by a person.
Commits what it writes, creates the integration branch and
switches to it, and drafts the three files only a person
places -- solution, techstack, constraints -- beside them.

commands.name: show
commands.description:
Fetch a lead and print it in one shape for 'intent --from':
azuredevops:1234 or github:56 through az or gh, a
suggestion:<cycle>/<finding>, a ready successor:<slug>, or a
file path. What came from outside is fenced as untrusted text.
Refuses a successor that is not ready. Jira is not read yet.

commands.name: new
commands.description:
Open a cycle: allocate its id, claim it where every worktree of
the repository looks, and create its directory. Refuses until
a declared stack is in place. In a sandbox, the cycle opens
beside the others. The intent skill runs it; you rarely type it.

commands.name: operate
commands.description:
Read production's errors from the telemetry store solution.md
declares, grouped by signature, personal data stripped, and
file each new one as a bug on the platform's tracker -- a lead.
Not filed again while open, or once a person dismissed it.
A person runs it; no pipeline does.
perspective show <name> --for <stage> [--cover]
One perspective for one stage -- intent, spec, plan, build or
verify: its method, the questions a fresh reader asks, its
rules and its evidence; with --cover, the author's short list.

commands.name: park
commands.description:
Compare a cycle's plan with every plan not yet built. A file
only another creates parks it: writes parked.md with what it
waits on, keeping its spec and plan. A file two plans both
name is reported. The plan skill runs it.

commands.name: perspectives
commands.description:
Which perspectives a cycle gets and why: always on, named by
the intent, or brought by the plan's declared files.

commands.name: pr-ready
commands.description:
Say whether a cycle may open a pull request, without opening
one. Exits 1 if not -- and always for a test run, a cycle
a local build judged. For every cycle, 'cycles --pr-ready'.

commands.name: report
commands.description:
The report a build ends on and the pull request leads with:
deviations, choices, what was changed at the person's request,
and the verification's concerns, as markdown. Merging the pull
request accepts them (D-181). Exits 1 when a deviation is
unsound.

commands.name: Reports
commands.description:
'suggestions' and 'harvest <aspect>' both print their answer and keep a copy under
.sdlc/reports/, because a person works through one of these rather than reading it
once. Nothing reads one back, ever: the directory ignores itself, and a report found
later is already out of date if a cycle has run since. Re-run the command rather than
trusting one.

commands.name: round
commands.description:
Append the next round to the artifact's findings ledger from
--from <file>: the readers' findings merged in, stamped with
the time and the hashes of what was judged, and chained to the
round before; suggestions go to the cycle's suggestions ledger,
each concern once under an S_ id. Refuses while anything above
is unsettled, a known finding restated in other words, a new
blocker with no one-line gist, a suggestion whose id or move
does not fit the cycle's, a new blocker citing a rule its
reader was not handed (D-174), and a new finding quoting its
rule in other words (D-177). --changed lists the sections
moved since the last round instead.
round prompt <id> <artifact> --dir <directory>
Write every reader's prompt for a round into a directory
outside the repository: shared.md, the block the rules reader
and every perspective open with, handed over as a system
prompt, and <reader>.prompt.md, each reader's own part. A
verify round after the cycle's first runs no perspective.
--reader
<name> writes one -- rules, diff on a verify, a perspective,
reconcile once the others have answered, or adjudicate on a
verify. --list names the readers and writes nothing.
round run <id> <artifact> --dir <directory> [--timeout <minutes>]
Start every reader whose prompt 'round prompt' wrote there and
that has no answer yet -- the rules reader first, alone, then
the rest -- each a fresh process from that directory, with no
tools and no MCP servers, marked as a reader, its answer
written beside its prompt (D-183). The verify adjudicator the
same way. Run it again to start a reader that returned
nothing, or the reconciler once its prompt is written. Exits
1 while a reader returned nothing; refuses with no host to
start a reader with.
round collect <id> <artifact> --dir <directory>
Read every reader's answer from that directory and draft
round.json beside them: new ids numbered past the ledgers,
the reconciler's restatements carried under the standing id,
each reader's usage carried for 'round --from' to record.
Lists the open findings no reader raised, whose dispositions
are yours: --answered <ids> and --withdrawn <ids> copy them
in from the ledger word for word, and anything unnamed stays
open. --host names the host the readers ran on.
round verdict <id> --from <file>
Write verify.md from the adjudicator's answer, byte for byte.
Refuses an answer that is not a verify document.

commands.name: scaffold
commands.description:
Write the solution skeleton -- a solution file, its projects, the
architecture tests and a reference slice -- and the .NET build
settings it compiles under. On a solution adopted into existing
code, never the skeleton: only the build settings files that
cycle's plan declares. Writes what is absent and leaves what is
there. Refuses without an approved plan: adoption writes no
code and no build settings.

commands.name: settings
commands.description:
How this solution is set to run: each key in solution.md,
declared or defaulted, and how to change it; what this
machine overrides; what this release fixes, and the decision
that fixes it. Points at constraints, stack and decisions
rather than repeating them. Writes nothing. Exits 1 when
solution.md cannot be read.

commands.name: sitrep
commands.description:
The morning's page, in Markdown: built cycles ready to merge
and in what order, with the ones expected to conflict;
what needs a person; what was held back and why; what is
waiting and going stale; the backlog -- every successor and
parked cycle, ready, waiting or stuck -- and what it cannot
see. Fetch the remote first: a built cycle is read from its
own branch. It starts nothing.
cycles --here [--for <step>]
Which cycle a skill given no id means: the cycles this
branch carries -- its own on a cycle branch, otherwise
those not yet on the integration branch -- that are ready
for to-plan, spec, plan, build, verify, remediate or pr.
Remediate takes a blocked, an escalated, or a passed cycle
whose verdict has not merged into the integration branch.
Exactly one:
prints its id alone and exits 0. Several, or none: lists
them and exits 1, so the person is asked, never guessed for.

commands.name: slices
commands.description:
Print the one git command that composes slices/<slug>/plan:
the integration branch with each sibling's plan branch merged
in, so one pull request admits every plan sliced together.
Refuses a sibling with no plan branch, plan or approval
ledger, and a plan that needs a file only a sibling's plan
creates; names the files two plans share. /sdlc:pr --plan
runs it.

commands.name: stack
commands.description:
What this solution declares it is built from: its defaults,
the stack rules switched on, and each build settings file --
whether the stack takes it and whether it is on disk. Then
what this release ships that the stack never mentions: a row
saying 'none' or false is an answer, no row is never asked.
Names the gap and closes none: a cycle's plan does that.

commands.name: status
commands.description:
Show the panel for a stage. Names beside the gate any recorded
decision the cycle departs from, and ends with the next
command and any successor that is ready or stuck.

commands.name: check
commands.description:
Refuse a successor file that cannot be read, one naming a
cycle or slug that does not exist, and a loop through
succeeds:. Exits 0 when the set is sound.
successor start <slug> <id>
In a cycle opened for a ready successor, on its plan branch:
refuse unless it is ready, then delete its file there. The
intent then records lead: successor:<slug>. /sdlc:intent
--from successor:<slug> runs it.

commands.name: successors
commands.description:
Every slice waiting on another's code, as a file in
.sdlc/successors/, and where each stands -- waiting, ready,
stuck behind an abandoned cycle, or unresolved -- worked out
from the record. Ready means everything it succeeds is on
the integration branch with a passing verify (D-125).

commands.name: suggestions
commands.description:
List the open non-blocking findings and what the builds
noticed, for one cycle or all, each concern once. --all lists
every status -- accepted, declined, answered, withdrawn --
with the cycle that decided it.
suggestions <id> --renumber
Give every suggestion id the cycle's ledger records twice --
two branches each numbering a new one, and a merge keeping
both -- the next free id, the first keeping its own (D-171).

commands.name: theme
commands.description:
The roles this solution's surfaces use and the values that
fill them -- the one place a colour or a typeface lives. With
no theme, a skeleton of roles for a person to fill; never a
value, because a colour is a brand's, not a tool's.

commands.name: tidy
commands.description:
The worktrees and local branches the framework opened whose
work has reached the integration branch: a plan branch once
its plan is there, a build once its verification passes there,
a slicing or sandbox once every cycle it carries is, anything
of an abandoned cycle, and anything of a cycle the harvest
ledger there records closed. Prints the removal for a person to run.
Deletes nothing, and leaves remote branches alone.

commands.name: unpark
commands.description:
Take a parked cycle back once everything it waits on merged
with a passing verify; its spec and plan are then read again
against what merged. Refuses one still waiting, saying why.

commands.name: upgrade
commands.description:
Everything that moves to take a release, in order, with what
each is on now: this machine's tool, the plugin, this
solution's pin and what 'sdlc init' writes, the factory's
images when it has one, and the open cycles still pinning an
older release. Without a release, the one this machine runs.
Always answered by this machine's release, never the pinned
one. Runs nothing.

commands.name: verify-chain
commands.description:
Re-establish the whole chain from the repository. Exits 1 if
it does not hold. This is the pull-request check. --base is the
target branch: a pull request changing only the cycle's
planning documents then gets the admission check -- plan,
approval, hashes, no verify.
verify-chain slices/<slug>/plan --base <branch>
The same check for a slicing's pull request: every cycle it
carries gets the admission check, its successors must be
sound, and a plan that needs a file only a sibling's plan
creates is refused (D-125).
verify-chain <branch> --base <branch>
On a branch that is no cycle's: no cycle needed when everything
it changes is the pin, what 'sdlc init' and 'sdlc factory'
write, answers in the declared stack to what the release asks,
and dependency versions. Each file must be what this release
writes from the base's copy, a pipeline step by step (D-133);
a dependency file may move only versions, of any size (D-134).
Anything else is refused: there is no chain.
admission <id> --base <branch>
Print true when a pull request carries only the cycle's
planning documents, and any successors, so a pipeline may
skip the build and tests; false for anything else. On

Print true when a pull request promotes the integration
branch or a release/* branch into another branch, so a
pipeline skips the chain; false when it targets the

commands.name: version
commands.description:

expects beside it. Inside a solution that pins another
release, every command -- this one too -- is answered by
the pinned release. With SDLC_DEV_BUILD set, by that build,

commands.name: cycles
commands.description:
What a build would take now -- approved, no verify, not
abandoned -- in the order to build it: the cycle the most
successors wait on first, then oldest. And every cycle held
back, with why: a cycle/<id>/... branch on the remote, or an
approval the gate no longer accepts. Deleting the branch
re-queues it. With an id, that cycle alone, and exits 1 with
why when it is not queued.

commands.name: decisions
commands.description:
The choices this solution has already settled, so a cycle reads
what was argued rather than arguing it again. CON_27 asks a cycle
departing from one to declare it where it arises. Names
the entries over the word budget, for a harvest to reword.

commands.name: show
commands.description:
One decision in full, standing or superseded: what a reader
handed only its headline asks for.

options.name: --owner
options.description:
CODEOWNERS line on GitHub and a required reviewer on
Azure DevOps; --self-approve lets an author's own vote
count on Azure DevOps, and on GitHub, which never counts
it, needs a team: --self-approve <team> lets that team
bypass the rules on a pull request.
branch <id> <kind>      Print the one git command that puts the working copy on the
branch a kind of work happens on -- plan, build,
build-unattended or forward -- creating it from the right
base: the integration branch once the plan is admitted to
it, before that the plan's own branch or the admission
branch carrying it. A plan only in a sandbox is refused
until 'sdlc admit' takes it out. 'sandbox' opens a
worktree on sandbox/<id> beside the repository, where every
cycle the work turns into is planned. 'plan --worktree'
opens the one cycle in a folder of its own. 'plan' without a
worktree refuses uncommitted work, which the switch would
carry, and a local plan branch whose ledger lacks the
approval the integration branch holds (D-123).
branch <id> remediate    Print the path of a worktree on the cycle's build branch -- the
one its pull request is from -- opening it when absent, from
the local branch or the remote's. Where remediation works, on
a blocked, escalated or passed cycle (D-185).
build [<id>]             Build it (D-178, D-184, D-187): commits the approval a person
placed in the sandbox if it is uncommitted, admits the plan
when it is only in a sandbox, opens the build's worktree beside
the repository, starts the build's own process there running

options.name: /sdlc
options.description:
never with permission checks off, never marked as a reader --
waits, and prints the report. Exits 0 on a pass, 1 on blocked
or escalated. With no id, every queued cycle in one process
started from here, each in a worktree of its own; a plan only
in a sandbox is queued only when named. Refuses when the
build's process cannot start, or ends without a report. The
one stage this binary runs rather than names a skill for.

commands.name: admit
commands.description:
In a sandbox: print the one git command that takes its
approved cycles' folders, and the successors it wrote, onto
cycle/<id>/plan for one or slices/sandbox-<id>/plan for
several, from the integration branch, in a worktree beside
the sandbox. What the gate does not let through stays. Refuses
outside a sandbox, with nothing approved, over uncommitted
changes in an approved cycle, and a plan that needs a file
only a sibling's plan creates. Abandoned cycles go with it as
records. 'sdlc build <id>' runs it, and /sdlc:pr --plan
runs it.

commands.name: areas
commands.description:
Each area areas.md defines: the files it covers today, the
rules and decisions carrying it, and entries naming an area
nobody defined. Exits 1 when an area covers no file, which
stops a round until it is fixed.

commands.name: backlog
commands.description:
Every successor and every parked cycle, in the waves they come
ready in -- ready now, then after one more merge, and so on
-- each with how to start it, and apart from them the stuck
and the unresolved. A view; it writes nothing (D-145).

commands.description:

branch a kind of work happens on -- plan, build,

base: the integration branch once the plan is admitted to

commands.description:

this solution's platform: pull requests only, nobody
bypassing, the pipeline required, squash into the
integration branch and merge commits into the default

commands.name: claude
commands.description:
Start Claude Code with the skills this release carries, which
in a solution that pins a release are that release's. Every
argument after 'claude' is Claude Code's, passed unchanged.

commands.name: constraints
commands.description:
An empty entry at the next free LOC_ id, for a rule a person
has in mind. Writes nothing; takes no wording.

commands.name: show
commands.description: One rule in full, in force or superseded.

commands.name: cycles
commands.description:

commands.description:
Where the build bent the approved documents, and the choices
it made that they left open: each entry in deviations.md,

commands.name: discard
commands.description:
In a sandbox: what throwing it away would lose. Each cycle
is empty, can go, is worth recording -- it fixed a decision,
or its readers raised something -- or is recorded already.
Prints the removal for a person to run once nothing worth
recording is unrecorded, and exits 1 until then. Deletes
nothing.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description:
Check this installation and this repository: the rules, git,
how many decisions every reader is handed,
adoption, which release wrote adoption's files against this
binary, line endings, every host's hook config, and the
pipeline that is the guarantee, and asks the platform
through az or gh whether branch policy requires it.
Reports and never repairs. Exits 1 if anything is wrong, a
policy that does not require the check included. What it
cannot see -- whether a host loaded the skills, or the
policy when the CLI is not signed in -- is marked
'elsewhere' and names who to ask. Before the first
cycle it ends with what a person still has to place, and the
one command that is next.

commands.name: abandon
commands.description: Print the record that stops a cycle, for a person to place.

commands.name: approval
commands.description:
Write the gate decision beside the ledger, for a person to
rename onto it. Writes no approval.

commands.name: harvest
commands.description:
Write drafts of constraints.md, decisions.md, techstack.md and
areas.md from the proposals marked [x] in a harvest proposal
file: each a copy of the file as it stands with only those
lines applied, refused if any rule, decision or stack row
would go missing. An area may be renamed, merged or removed.

commands.name: solution
commands.description:
Write the whole solution.md beside itself, for a person
to rename onto it. Carries every key through as
recorded and the prose through unchanged, so the rename
cannot reclassify the solution or cost anybody what they
wrote. --approval, --coverage-floor and --standard each
change their one key when asked, and say so.

commands.name: techstack
commands.description:
Write the declared stack beside itself, for an edit a person
renames into place: a copy of it, or the framework's default
where there is none yet, with every stack rule listed and on.
The default also lists the five .NET build settings files, one
row each: on where the repository held no code, off where it
did. A row not true here says 'none' rather than being
deleted. On a copy, names what this release ships that the
stack never mentions, and adds none of it. Also reports the
options menu: every concern the shipped profiles know about,
what each declares, every stack rule, and what each build
settings file does and costs. The menu is never renamed into
place.

commands.name: Environment
commands.description:
SDLC_DEV_BUILD           A directory holding a build of sdlc nobody published. Every
command is handed to it instead of the pinned release, it
calls itself <release>-local, and no cycle it judged opens a
pull request. For testing a change to the framework.

commands.name: evidence
commands.description:
Record what a build produced: its base commit, the commit it is

coverage. Verify reads only this. The summary records the

not committed; the diff is rebuilt from the two commits and
never committed (D-124). Retires a blocked verify.md, and
refuses while any other verdict stands (D-161) -- unless

that passed (D-185).

commands.description:

recorded evidence holds, and tests it says passed that did not.
Reports only; always exits 0.

commands.description:

--unattended against the integration branch -- every queued

commands.name: findings
commands.description:

commands.name: gate
commands.description: Say whether a cycle's build may run. Exits 1 if not.

harvest'. Proposes; writes nothing that binds. --cycles reads
those cycles alone and leaves the rest for a later sitting;

harvest constraints, harvest decisions, harvest suggestions,
harvest stack, harvest areas.

names have answered it, with the concerns under '## Watch' and
'## Ignored' tallied and the suggestions under '## Declined'
kept. Closes nothing. Refuses while the draft is still beside
its file.

commands.name: close
commands.description:
Close every completed cycle whose five aspects have all been
answered: record what later harvests need, and on a new
harvest/<date> branch commit the removal of their folders with
the ledger and the records a person placed. Pushes nothing.
Refuses, naming what each cycle still needs, while nothing can
close; while a draft is still beside its file; and anywhere
but the integration branch.

Write one prompt per completed cycle and document with findings
in the aspect's sitting, constraints unless given, each that
document's findings and the question that groups them, and
start one fresh reader for each, its answer written beside its
prompt (D-183).

Write and start the two readers that review one aspect's
sitting: one handed the marked proposal file, the aspect's
draft and solution.md; one handed the aspect's report and the
proposal file. The newest of each in .sdlc/reports unless
--proposals names the file.

commands.name: help
commands.description: This text. So does --help after any command.

commands.name: hook
commands.description:

starts that its skills are another release. Reads the host's
payload on stdin and writes its decision on stdout.
Hosts: claude, copilot, antigravity.

commands.name: init
commands.description:

Commits what it writes, creates the integration branch and
switches to it, and drafts the three files only a person
places -- solution, techstack, constraints -- beside them.

commands.name: show
commands.description:

suggestion:<cycle>/<finding>, a ready successor:<slug>, or a
file path. What came from outside is fenced as untrusted text.
Refuses a successor that is not ready. Jira is not read yet.

commands.name: new
commands.description:

the repository looks, and create its directory. Refuses until
a declared stack is in place. In a sandbox, the cycle opens
beside the others. The intent skill runs it; you rarely type it.

commands.name: operate
commands.description:

declares, grouped by signature, personal data stripped, and
file each new one as a bug on the platform's tracker -- a lead.
Not filed again while open, or once a person dismissed it.
A person runs it; no pipeline does.

One perspective for one stage -- intent, spec, plan, build or
verify: its method, the questions a fresh reader asks, its
rules and its evidence; with --cover, the author's short list.

commands.description:

only another creates parks it: writes parked.md with what it
waits on, keeping its spec and plan. A file two plans both
name is reported. The plan skill runs it.

commands.name: perspectives
commands.description:

commands.description:

one. Exits 1 if not -- and always for a test run, a cycle
a local build judged. For every cycle, 'cycles --pr-ready'.

commands.name: report
commands.description:

and the verification's concerns, as markdown. Merging the pull
request accepts them (D-181). Exits 1 when a deviation is

commands.description:

trusting one.

commands.description:

each concern once under an S_ id. Refuses while anything above
is unsettled, a known finding restated in other words, a new
blocker with no one-line gist, a suggestion whose id or move
does not fit the cycle's, a new blocker citing a rule its
reader was not handed (D-174), and a new finding quoting its
rule in other words (D-177). --changed lists the sections
moved since the last round instead.

Write every reader's prompt for a round into a directory
outside the repository: shared.md, the block the rules reader
and every perspective open with, handed over as a system
prompt, and <reader>.prompt.md, each reader's own part. A
verify round after the cycle's first runs no perspective.
--reader
<name> writes one -- rules, diff on a verify, a perspective,
reconcile once the others have answered, or adjudicate on a
verify. --list names the readers and writes nothing.

that has no answer yet -- the rules reader first, alone, then
the rest -- each a fresh process from that directory, with no
tools and no MCP servers, marked as a reader, its answer
written beside its prompt (D-183). The verify adjudicator the
same way. Run it again to start a reader that returned
nothing, or the reconciler once its prompt is written. Exits
1 while a reader returned nothing; refuses with no host to
start a reader with.
round collect <id> <artifact> --dir <directory>
Read every reader's answer from that directory and draft
round.json beside them: new ids numbered past the ledgers,
the reconciler's restatements carried under the standing id,
each reader's usage carried for 'round --from' to record.
Lists the open findings no reader raised, whose dispositions
are yours: --answered <ids> and --withdrawn <ids> copy them
in from the ledger word for word, and anything unnamed stays
open. --host names the host the readers ran on.

Write verify.md from the adjudicator's answer, byte for byte.
Refuses an answer that is not a verify document.

commands.description:

commands.description:

and in what order, with the ones expected to conflict;
what needs a person; what was held back and why; what is
waiting and going stale; the backlog -- every successor and
parked cycle, ready, waiting or stuck -- and what it cannot
see. Fetch the remote first: a built cycle is read from its
own branch. It starts nothing.

Which cycle a skill given no id means: the cycles this
branch carries -- its own on a cycle branch, otherwise
those not yet on the integration branch -- that are ready
for to-plan, spec, plan, build, verify, remediate or pr.

whose verdict has not merged into the integration branch.
Exactly one:

commands.description:

in, so one pull request admits every plan sliced together.
Refuses a sibling with no plan branch, plan or approval
ledger, and a plan that needs a file only a sibling's plan
creates; names the files two plans share. /sdlc:pr --plan

commands.description:

Names the gap and closes none: a cycle's plan does that.

commands.name: status
commands.description:

commands.description:

commands.description:

commands.description:

commands.name: tidy
commands.description:

work has reached the integration branch: a plan branch once
its plan is there, a build once its verification passes there,
a slicing or sandbox once every cycle it carries is, anything
of an abandoned cycle, and anything of a cycle the harvest
ledger there records closed. Prints the removal for a person to run.
Deletes nothing, and leaves remote branches alone.

commands.description:

with a passing verify; its spec and plan are then read again
against what merged. Refuses one still waiting, saying why.

commands.name: upgrade
commands.description:
Everything that moves to take a release, in order, with what
each is on now: this machine's tool, the plugin, this
solution's pin and what 'sdlc init' writes, the factory's
images when it has one, and the open cycles still pinning an
older release. Without a release, the one this machine runs.
Always answered by this machine's release, never the pinned
one. Runs nothing.

commands.name: verify-chain
commands.description:

target branch: a pull request changing only the cycle's
planning documents then gets the admission check -- plan,

write, answers in the declared stack to what the release asks,

writes from the base's copy, a pipeline step by step (D-133);

Print true when a pull request carries only the cycle's

options.name: /sdlc

never with permission checks off, never marked as a reader --

or escalated. With no id, every queued cycle in one process

in a sandbox is queued only when named. Refuses when the

commands.name: admit
commands.description:

approved cycles' folders, and the successors it wrote, onto
cycle/<id>/plan for one or slices/sandbox-<id>/plan for
several, from the integration branch, in a worktree beside

changes in an approved cycle, and a plan that needs a file
only a sibling's plan creates. Abandoned cycles go with it as
records. 'sdlc build <id>' runs it, and /sdlc:pr --plan
runs it.

commands.name: areas
commands.description:
Each area areas.md defines: the files it covers today, the
rules and decisions carrying it, and entries naming an area
nobody defined. Exits 1 when an area covers no file, which
stops a round until it is fixed.

commands.name: backlog
commands.description:
Every successor and every parked cycle, in the waves they come
ready in -- ready now, then after one more merge, and so on
-- each with how to start it, and apart from them the stuck
and the unresolved. A view; it writes nothing (D-145).

commands.name: branch
commands.description:
Print the one git command that puts the working copy on the
branch a kind of work happens on -- plan, build,
build-unattended or forward -- creating it from the right
base: the integration branch once the plan is admitted to
it, before that the plan's own branch or the admission
branch carrying it. A plan only in a sandbox is refused
until 'sdlc admit' takes it out. 'sandbox' opens a
worktree on sandbox/<id> beside the repository, where every
cycle the work turns into is planned. 'plan --worktree'
opens the one cycle in a folder of its own. 'plan' without a
worktree refuses uncommitted work, which the switch would
carry, and a local plan branch whose ledger lacks the
approval the integration branch holds (D-123).

commands.name: branch-policy
commands.description:

this solution's platform: pull requests only, nobody
bypassing, the pipeline required, squash into the
integration branch and merge commits into the default
branch. Applies nothing; run them as an administrator.

commands.description:

placed in the sandbox if it is uncommitted, admits the plan
when it is only in a sandbox, opens the build's worktree beside
the repository, starts the build's own process there running

never with permission checks off, never marked as a reader --
waits, and prints the report. Exits 0 on a pass, 1 on blocked

started from here, each in a worktree of its own; a plan only

commands.name: claude
commands.description:

in a solution that pins a release are that release's. Every
argument after 'claude' is Claude Code's, passed unchanged.

commands.name: constraints
commands.description:

has in mind. Writes nothing; takes no wording.

commands.name: show
commands.description: One rule in full, in force or superseded.

commands.name: cycles
commands.description:

abandoned -- in the order to build it: the cycle the most
successors wait on first, then oldest. And every cycle held
back, with why: a cycle/<id>/... branch on the remote, or an
approval the gate no longer accepts. Deleting the branch
re-queues it. With an id, that cycle alone, and exits 1 with
why when it is not queued.

commands.name: decisions
commands.description:

what was argued rather than arguing it again. CON_27 asks a cycle
departing from one to declare it where it arises. Names
the entries over the word budget, for a harvest to reword.

commands.name: show
commands.description:
One decision in full, standing or superseded: what a reader
handed only its headline asks for.

commands.name: deviations
commands.description:

the approved text, takes a claimed file or narrows a criterion.

commands.name: discard
commands.description:

is empty, can go, is worth recording -- it fixed a decision,
or its readers raised something -- or is recorded already.
Prints the removal for a person to run once nothing worth
recording is unrecorded, and exits 1 until then. Deletes
nothing.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description:
Check this installation and this repository: the rules, git,
how many decisions every reader is handed,
adoption, which release wrote adoption's files against this
binary, line endings, every host's hook config, and the
pipeline that is the guarantee, and asks the platform
through az or gh whether branch policy requires it.
Reports and never repairs. Exits 1 if anything is wrong, a
policy that does not require the check included. What it
cannot see -- whether a host loaded the skills, or the
policy when the CLI is not signed in -- is marked
'elsewhere' and names who to ask. Before the first
cycle it ends with what a person still has to place, and the
one command that is next.

commands.name: approval
commands.description:
Write the gate decision beside the ledger, for a person to
rename onto it. Writes no approval.

commands.name: harvest
commands.description:

areas.md from the proposals marked [x] in a harvest proposal
file: each a copy of the file as it stands with only those
lines applied, refused if any rule, decision or stack row
would go missing. An area may be renamed, merged or removed.

commands.name: solution
commands.description:
Write the whole solution.md beside itself, for a person
to rename onto it. Carries every key through as
recorded and the prose through unchanged, so the rename
cannot reclassify the solution or cost anybody what they
wrote. --approval, --coverage-floor and --standard each
change their one key when asked, and say so.

commands.name: techstack
commands.description:
Write the declared stack beside itself, for an edit a person
renames into place: a copy of it, or the framework's default
where there is none yet, with every stack rule listed and on.
The default also lists the five .NET build settings files, one
row each: on where the repository held no code, off where it
did. A row not true here says 'none' rather than being
deleted. On a copy, names what this release ships that the
stack never mentions, and adds none of it. Also reports the
options menu: every concern the shipped profiles know about,
what each declares, every stack rule, and what each build
settings file does and costs. The menu is never renamed into
place.

command is handed to it instead of the pinned release, it
calls itself <release>-local, and no cycle it judged opens a
pull request. For testing a change to the framework.

commands.description:

commands.description:

Reports only; always exits 0.

commands.description: Say whether a cycle's build may run. Exits 1 if not.

same way. Run it again to start a reader that returned
nothing, or the reconciler once its prompt is written. Exits

start a reader with.

count on Azure DevOps, and on GitHub, which never counts
it, needs a team: --self-approve <team> lets that team
bypass the rules on a pull request.

commands.name: build
commands.description:
Build it (D-178, D-184, D-187): commits the approval a person
placed in the sandbox if it is uncommitted, admits the plan
when it is only in a sandbox, opens the build's worktree beside
the repository, starts the build's own process there running
/sdlc:build <id> --unattended -- headless, its tools named,
never with permission checks off, never marked as a reader --
waits, and prints the report. Exits 0 on a pass, 1 on blocked
or escalated. With no id, every queued cycle in one process
started from here, each in a worktree of its own; a plan only
in a sandbox is queued only when named. Refuses when the
build's process cannot start, or ends without a report. The
one stage this binary runs rather than names a skill for.

commands.name: claude
commands.description:
Start Claude Code with the skills this release carries, which
in a solution that pins a release are that release's. Every
argument after 'claude' is Claude Code's, passed unchanged.

commands.name: constraints
commands.description:
An empty entry at the next free LOC_ id, for a rule a person
has in mind. Writes nothing; takes no wording.

commands.name: show
commands.description: One rule in full, in force or superseded.

commands.name: cycles
commands.description:
What a build would take now -- approved, no verify, not
abandoned -- in the order to build it: the cycle the most
successors wait on first, then oldest. And every cycle held
back, with why: a cycle/<id>/... branch on the remote, or an
approval the gate no longer accepts. Deleting the branch
re-queues it. With an id, that cycle alone, and exits 1 with
why when it is not queued.

commands.name: decisions
commands.description:
The choices this solution has already settled, so a cycle reads
what was argued rather than arguing it again. CON_27 asks a cycle
departing from one to declare it where it arises. Names
the entries over the word budget, for a harvest to reword.

commands.name: show
commands.description:
One decision in full, standing or superseded: what a reader
handed only its headline asks for.

commands.name: deviations
commands.description:
Where the build bent the approved documents, and the choices
it made that they left open: each entry in deviations.md,
whether it is in force or was changed at the person's request,
and anything wrong with it. Exits 1 while a deviation misquotes
the approved text, takes a claimed file or narrows a criterion.

commands.name: discard
commands.description:
In a sandbox: what throwing it away would lose. Each cycle
is empty, can go, is worth recording -- it fixed a decision,
or its readers raised something -- or is recorded already.
Prints the removal for a person to run once nothing worth
recording is unrecorded, and exits 1 until then. Deletes
nothing.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description:
Check this installation and this repository: the rules, git,
how many decisions every reader is handed,
adoption, which release wrote adoption's files against this
binary, line endings, every host's hook config, and the
pipeline that is the guarantee, and asks the platform
through az or gh whether branch policy requires it.
Reports and never repairs. Exits 1 if anything is wrong, a
policy that does not require the check included. What it
cannot see -- whether a host loaded the skills, or the
policy when the CLI is not signed in -- is marked
'elsewhere' and names who to ask. Before the first
cycle it ends with what a person still has to place, and the
one command that is next.

commands.name: abandon
commands.description: Print the record that stops a cycle, for a person to place.

commands.name: harvest
commands.description:
Write drafts of constraints.md, decisions.md, techstack.md and
areas.md from the proposals marked [x] in a harvest proposal
file: each a copy of the file as it stands with only those
lines applied, refused if any rule, decision or stack row
would go missing. An area may be renamed, merged or removed.

commands.name: solution
commands.description:
Write the whole solution.md beside itself, for a person
to rename onto it. Carries every key through as
recorded and the prose through unchanged, so the rename
cannot reclassify the solution or cost anybody what they
wrote. --approval, --coverage-floor and --standard each
change their one key when asked, and say so.

commands.name: techstack
commands.description:
Write the declared stack beside itself, for an edit a person
renames into place: a copy of it, or the framework's default
where there is none yet, with every stack rule listed and on.
The default also lists the five .NET build settings files, one
row each: on where the repository held no code, off where it
did. A row not true here says 'none' rather than being
deleted. On a copy, names what this release ships that the
stack never mentions, and adds none of it. Also reports the
options menu: every concern the shipped profiles know about,
what each declares, every stack rule, and what each build
settings file does and costs. The menu is never renamed into
place.

commands.name: Environment
commands.description:
SDLC_DEV_BUILD           A directory holding a build of sdlc nobody published. Every
command is handed to it instead of the pinned release, it
calls itself <release>-local, and no cycle it judged opens a
pull request. For testing a change to the framework.

commands.name: evidence
commands.description:
Record what a build produced: its base commit, the commit it is
at, the diff between them, a normalised test summary and the
coverage. Verify reads only this. The summary records the
platform the tests ran on. Refuses code outside .sdlc/ that is
not committed; the diff is rebuilt from the two commits and
never committed (D-124). Retires a blocked verify.md, and
refuses while any other verdict stands (D-161) -- unless
--retire-pass, when a person asked for a change to a cycle
that passed (D-185).

commands.name: check
commands.description:
List what verify.md cites in backticks that none of the
recorded evidence holds, and tests it says passed that did not.
Reports only; always exits 0.

commands.name: factory
commands.description:
Write the factory's pipeline for the recorded platform: a run
a person starts, never a schedule, of /sdlc:build
--unattended against the integration branch -- every queued
cycle, or the one named as its input -- one run at a time,
six hours at most, proving the hooks refuse before it builds,
and publishing the sitrep. It never merges. Refuses on a
local solution.

commands.name: findings
commands.description:
What the interrogations said, per artifact, each finding at the
disposition that stands.

commands.name: gate
commands.description: Say whether a cycle's build may run. Exits 1 if not.

commands.name: harvest
commands.description:
One aspect -- constraints, decisions, suggestions, stack or
areas -- for the completed cycles that have not answered it,
ending with the proposal file a person marks for 'draft
harvest'. Proposes; writes nothing that binds. --cycles reads
those cycles alone and leaves the rest for a later sitting;
the rule counts stay the whole completed record's. So:
harvest constraints, harvest decisions, harvest suggestions,
harvest stack, harvest areas.
harvest record <aspect> <file>
Once the aspect's draft is renamed into place: record in
.sdlc/harvested.json that the cycles the file's '## Cycles'
names have answered it, with the concerns under '## Watch' and
'## Ignored' tallied and the suggestions under '## Declined'
kept. Closes nothing. Refuses while the draft is still beside
its file.

commands.name: close
commands.description:
Close every completed cycle whose five aspects have all been
answered: record what later harvests need, and on a new
harvest/<date> branch commit the removal of their folders with
the ledger and the records a person placed. Pushes nothing.
Refuses, naming what each cycle still needs, while nothing can
close; while a draft is still beside its file; and anywhere
but the integration branch.

in the aspect's sitting, constraints unless given, each that
document's findings and the question that groups them, and
start one fresh reader for each, its answer written beside its
prompt (D-183).

Write and start the two readers that review one aspect's
sitting: one handed the marked proposal file, the aspect's
draft and solution.md; one handed the aspect's report and the
proposal file. The newest of each in .sdlc/reports unless
--proposals names the file.

commands.name: help
commands.description: This text. So does --help after any command.

commands.name: hook
commands.description:

starts that its skills are another release. Reads the host's
payload on stdin and writes its decision on stdout.
Hosts: claude, copilot, antigravity.

commands.name: init
commands.description:

Commits what it writes, creates the integration branch and
switches to it, and drafts the three files only a person
places -- solution, techstack, constraints -- beside them.

commands.name: show
commands.description:

file path. What came from outside is fenced as untrusted text.
Refuses a successor that is not ready. Jira is not read yet.

a declared stack is in place. In a sandbox, the cycle opens
beside the others. The intent skill runs it; you rarely type it.

file each new one as a bug on the platform's tracker -- a lead.

A person runs it; no pipeline does.

One perspective for one stage -- intent, spec, plan, build or
verify: its method, the questions a fresh reader asks, its
rules and its evidence; with --cover, the author's short list.

commands.name: park
commands.description:

waits on, keeping its spec and plan. A file two plans both
name is reported. The plan skill runs it.

commands.name: perspectives
commands.description:

commands.name: pr-ready
commands.description:

one. Exits 1 if not -- and always for a test run, a cycle

commands.name: report
commands.description:

verify. --list names the readers and writes nothing.

tools and no MCP servers, marked as a reader, its answer

same way. Run it again to start a reader that returned
nothing, or the reconciler once its prompt is written. Exits
1 while a reader returned nothing; refuses with no host to
start a reader with.

the reconciler's restatements carried under the standing id,
each reader's usage carried for 'round --from' to record.
Lists the open findings no reader raised, whose dispositions
are yours: --answered <ids> and --withdrawn <ids> copy them
in from the ledger word for word, and anything unnamed stays
open. --host names the host the readers ran on.

Refuses an answer that is not a verify document.

cycle's plan declares. Writes what is absent and leaves what is
there. Refuses without an approved plan: adoption writes no
code and no build settings.

commands.description:

declared or defaulted, and how to change it; what this
machine overrides; what this release fixes, and the decision
that fixes it. Points at constraints, stack and decisions
rather than repeating them. Writes nothing. Exits 1 when

commands.description:

and in what order, with the ones expected to conflict;
what needs a person; what was held back and why; what is
waiting and going stale; the backlog -- every successor and
parked cycle, ready, waiting or stuck -- and what it cannot
see. Fetch the remote first: a built cycle is read from its
own branch. It starts nothing.

Which cycle a skill given no id means: the cycles this
branch carries -- its own on a cycle branch, otherwise
those not yet on the integration branch -- that are ready
for to-plan, spec, plan, build, verify, remediate or pr.
Remediate takes a blocked, an escalated, or a passed cycle
whose verdict has not merged into the integration branch.
Exactly one:
prints its id alone and exits 0. Several, or none: lists
them and exits 1, so the person is asked, never guessed for.

commands.name: slices
commands.description:

the integration branch with each sibling's plan branch merged
in, so one pull request admits every plan sliced together.
Refuses a sibling with no plan branch, plan or approval
ledger, and a plan that needs a file only a sibling's plan
creates; names the files two plans share. /sdlc:pr --plan
runs it.

commands.description:

the stack rules switched on, and each build settings file --
whether the stack takes it and whether it is on disk. Then

saying 'none' or false is an answer, no row is never asked.
Names the gap and closes none: a cycle's plan does that.

commands.name: status
commands.description:

decision the cycle departs from, and ends with the next
command and any successor that is ready or stuck.

commands.name: check
commands.description:
Refuse a successor file that cannot be read, one naming a
cycle or slug that does not exist, and a loop through
succeeds:. Exits 0 when the set is sound.

In a cycle opened for a ready successor, on its plan branch:
refuse unless it is ready, then delete its file there. The
intent then records lead: successor:<slug>. /sdlc:intent
--from successor:<slug> runs it.

commands.name: successors
commands.description:
Every slice waiting on another's code, as a file in
.sdlc/successors/, and where each stands -- waiting, ready,
stuck behind an abandoned cycle, or unresolved -- worked out
from the record. Ready means everything it succeeds is on
the integration branch with a passing verify (D-125).

commands.name: suggestions
commands.description:
List the open non-blocking findings and what the builds
noticed, for one cycle or all, each concern once. --all lists
every status -- accepted, declined, answered, withdrawn --
with the cycle that decided it.
suggestions <id> --renumber
Give every suggestion id the cycle's ledger records twice --
two branches each numbering a new one, and a merge keeping
both -- the next free id, the first keeping its own (D-171).

commands.name: theme
commands.description:
The roles this solution's surfaces use and the values that
fill them -- the one place a colour or a typeface lives. With
no theme, a skeleton of roles for a person to fill; never a
value, because a colour is a brand's, not a tool's.

commands.name: tidy
commands.description:
The worktrees and local branches the framework opened whose
work has reached the integration branch: a plan branch once
its plan is there, a build once its verification passes there,
a slicing or sandbox once every cycle it carries is, anything
of an abandoned cycle, and anything of a cycle the harvest
ledger there records closed. Prints the removal for a person to run.
Deletes nothing, and leaves remote branches alone.

commands.name: unpark
commands.description:
Take a parked cycle back once everything it waits on merged
with a passing verify; its spec and plan are then read again
against what merged. Refuses one still waiting, saying why.

commands.name: upgrade
commands.description:
Everything that moves to take a release, in order, with what
each is on now: this machine's tool, the plugin, this
solution's pin and what 'sdlc init' writes, the factory's
images when it has one, and the open cycles still pinning an
older release. Without a release, the one this machine runs.
Always answered by this machine's release, never the pinned
one. Runs nothing.

commands.name: verify-chain
commands.description:
Re-establish the whole chain from the repository. Exits 1 if
it does not hold. This is the pull-request check. --base is the
target branch: a pull request changing only the cycle's
planning documents then gets the admission check -- plan,
approval, hashes, no verify.
verify-chain slices/<slug>/plan --base <branch>
The same check for a slicing's pull request: every cycle it
carries gets the admission check, its successors must be
sound, and a plan that needs a file only a sibling's plan
creates is refused (D-125).
verify-chain <branch> --base <branch>
On a branch that is no cycle's: no cycle needed when everything
it changes is the pin, what 'sdlc init' and 'sdlc factory'
write, answers in the declared stack to what the release asks,
and dependency versions. Each file must be what this release
writes from the base's copy, a pipeline step by step (D-133);
a dependency file may move only versions, of any size (D-134).
Anything else is refused: there is no chain.
admission <id> --base <branch>
Print true when a pull request carries only the cycle's
planning documents, and any successors, so a pipeline may
skip the build and tests; false for anything else. On
slices/<slug>/plan, true when it carries only cycles'
planning and successors. Always exits 0.
promotion <source> --base <target>
Print true when a pull request promotes the integration
branch or a release/* branch into another branch, so a
pipeline skips the chain; false when it targets the
integration branch or a release branch. Exits 1 when any
other branch targets another branch.

commands.name: version
commands.description:
Which version of the gate this is, and which versions it
expects beside it. Inside a solution that pins another
release, every command -- this one too -- is answered by
the pinned release. With SDLC_DEV_BUILD set, by that build,
which calls itself <release>-local.

changes in an approved cycle, and a plan that needs a file
only a sibling's plan creates. Abandoned cycles go with it as
records. 'sdlc build <id>' runs it, and /sdlc:pr --plan
runs it.

commands.name: areas

Each area areas.md defines: the files it covers today, the
rules and decisions carrying it, and entries naming an area
nobody defined. Exits 1 when an area covers no file, which
stops a round until it is fixed.

commands.name: backlog
commands.description:
Every successor and every parked cycle, in the waves they come
ready in -- ready now, then after one more merge, and so on
-- each with how to start it, and apart from them the stuck
and the unresolved. A view; it writes nothing (D-145).

bypassing, the pipeline required, squash into the

binary, line endings, every host's hook config, and the
pipeline that is the guarantee, and asks the platform
through az or gh whether branch policy requires it.
Reports and never repairs. Exits 1 if anything is wrong, a
policy that does not require the check included. What it
cannot see -- whether a host loaded the skills, or the
policy when the CLI is not signed in -- is marked
'elsewhere' and names who to ask. Before the first
cycle it ends with what a person still has to place, and the
one command that is next.

commands.name: abandon
commands.description: Print the record that stops a cycle, for a person to place.

commands.name: approval
commands.description:
Write the gate decision beside the ledger, for a person to
rename onto it. Writes no approval.

commands.name: harvest
commands.description:
Write drafts of constraints.md, decisions.md, techstack.md and
areas.md from the proposals marked [x] in a harvest proposal
file: each a copy of the file as it stands with only those
lines applied, refused if any rule, decision or stack row
would go missing. An area may be renamed, merged or removed.

commands.name: techstack
commands.description:
Write the declared stack beside itself, for an edit a person
renames into place: a copy of it, or the framework's default
where there is none yet, with every stack rule listed and on.
The default also lists the five .NET build settings files, one
row each: on where the repository held no code, off where it
did. A row not true here says 'none' rather than being
deleted. On a copy, names what this release ships that the
stack never mentions, and adds none of it. Also reports the
options menu: every concern the shipped profiles know about,
what each declares, every stack rule, and what each build
settings file does and costs. The menu is never renamed into
place.

commands.name: Environment
commands.description:
SDLC_DEV_BUILD           A directory holding a build of sdlc nobody published. Every
command is handed to it instead of the pinned release, it
calls itself <release>-local, and no cycle it judged opens a
pull request. For testing a change to the framework.

commands.name: evidence
commands.description:
Record what a build produced: its base commit, the commit it is
at, the diff between them, a normalised test summary and the
coverage. Verify reads only this. The summary records the
platform the tests ran on. Refuses code outside .sdlc/ that is
not committed; the diff is rebuilt from the two commits and
never committed (D-124). Retires a blocked verify.md, and
refuses while any other verdict stands (D-161) -- unless
--retire-pass, when a person asked for a change to a cycle
that passed (D-185).

commands.name: check
commands.description:
List what verify.md cites in backticks that none of the
recorded evidence holds, and tests it says passed that did not.
Reports only; always exits 0.

commands.name: factory
commands.description:
Write the factory's pipeline for the recorded platform: a run
a person starts, never a schedule, of /sdlc:build
--unattended against the integration branch -- every queued
cycle, or the one named as its input -- one run at a time,
six hours at most, proving the hooks refuse before it builds,
and publishing the sitrep. It never merges. Refuses on a
local solution.

commands.name: findings
commands.description:
What the interrogations said, per artifact, each finding at the
disposition that stands.

commands.name: gate
commands.description: Say whether a cycle's build may run. Exits 1 if not.

commands.name: harvest
commands.description:
One aspect -- constraints, decisions, suggestions, stack or
areas -- for the completed cycles that have not answered it,
ending with the proposal file a person marks for 'draft
harvest'. Proposes; writes nothing that binds. --cycles reads
those cycles alone and leaves the rest for a later sitting;
the rule counts stay the whole completed record's. So:
harvest constraints, harvest decisions, harvest suggestions,
harvest stack, harvest areas.
harvest record <aspect> <file>
Once the aspect's draft is renamed into place: record in
.sdlc/harvested.json that the cycles the file's '## Cycles'
names have answered it, with the concerns under '## Watch' and
'## Ignored' tallied and the suggestions under '## Declined'
kept. Closes nothing. Refuses while the draft is still beside
its file.

commands.name: close
commands.description:
Close every completed cycle whose five aspects have all been
answered: record what later harvests need, and on a new
harvest/<date> branch commit the removal of their folders with
the ledger and the records a person placed. Pushes nothing.
Refuses, naming what each cycle still needs, while nothing can
close; while a draft is still beside its file; and anywhere
but the integration branch.

Write one prompt per completed cycle and document with findings
in the aspect's sitting, constraints unless given, each that
document's findings and the question that groups them, and
start one fresh reader for each, its answer written beside its
prompt (D-183).
harvest review <aspect> --dir <directory> [--proposals <file>]
Write and start the two readers that review one aspect's
sitting: one handed the marked proposal file, the aspect's
draft and solution.md; one handed the aspect's report and the
proposal file. The newest of each in .sdlc/reports unless
--proposals names the file.

commands.name: help
commands.description: This text. So does --help after any command.

commands.name: hook
commands.description:
Judge a tool call, or a turn that is ending, or say as a session
starts that its skills are another release. Reads the host's
payload on stdin and writes its decision on stdout.
Hosts: claude, copilot, antigravity.

commands.name: init
commands.description:
Adopt the framework into this repository. Run by a person.
Commits what it writes, creates the integration branch and
switches to it, and drafts the three files only a person
places -- solution, techstack, constraints -- beside them.

commands.name: show
commands.description:
Fetch a lead and print it in one shape for 'intent --from':
azuredevops:1234 or github:56 through az or gh, a
suggestion:<cycle>/<finding>, a ready successor:<slug>, or a
file path. What came from outside is fenced as untrusted text.
Refuses a successor that is not ready. Jira is not read yet.

commands.name: new
commands.description:
Open a cycle: allocate its id, claim it where every worktree of
the repository looks, and create its directory. Refuses until
a declared stack is in place. In a sandbox, the cycle opens
beside the others. The intent skill runs it; you rarely type it.

commands.name: operate
commands.description:
Read production's errors from the telemetry store solution.md
declares, grouped by signature, personal data stripped, and
file each new one as a bug on the platform's tracker -- a lead.
Not filed again while open, or once a person dismissed it.
A person runs it; no pipeline does.

One perspective for one stage -- intent, spec, plan, build or
verify: its method, the questions a fresh reader asks, its
rules and its evidence; with --cover, the author's short list.

commands.name: park
commands.description:

only another creates parks it: writes parked.md with what it
waits on, keeping its spec and plan. A file two plans both
name is reported. The plan skill runs it.

commands.name: perspectives
commands.description:
Which perspectives a cycle gets and why: always on, named by
the intent, or brought by the plan's declared files.

commands.name: pr-ready
commands.description:
Say whether a cycle may open a pull request, without opening
one. Exits 1 if not -- and always for a test run, a cycle
a local build judged. For every cycle, 'cycles --pr-ready'.

commands.name: report
commands.description:

trusting one.

commands.description:

is unsettled, a known finding restated in other words, a new
blocker with no one-line gist, a suggestion whose id or move
does not fit the cycle's, a new blocker citing a rule its
reader was not handed (D-174), and a new finding quoting its
rule in other words (D-177). --changed lists the sections
moved since the last round instead.

Write every reader's prompt for a round into a directory
outside the repository: shared.md, the block the rules reader
and every perspective open with, handed over as a system
prompt, and <reader>.prompt.md, each reader's own part. A
verify round after the cycle's first runs no perspective.
--reader
<name> writes one -- rules, diff on a verify, a perspective,
reconcile once the others have answered, or adjudicate on a
verify. --list names the readers and writes nothing.

Start every reader whose prompt 'round prompt' wrote there and
that has no answer yet -- the rules reader first, alone, then
the rest -- each a fresh process from that directory, with no
tools and no MCP servers, marked as a reader, its answer
written beside its prompt (D-183). The verify adjudicator the
same way. Run it again to start a reader that returned
nothing, or the reconciler once its prompt is written. Exits
1 while a reader returned nothing; refuses with no host to
start a reader with.
round collect <id> <artifact> --dir <directory>
Read every reader's answer from that directory and draft
round.json beside them: new ids numbered past the ledgers,
the reconciler's restatements carried under the standing id,
each reader's usage carried for 'round --from' to record.
Lists the open findings no reader raised, whose dispositions
are yours: --answered <ids> and --withdrawn <ids> copy them
in from the ledger word for word, and anything unnamed stays

Exactly one:

commands.description:

value, because a colour is a brand's, not a tool's.

commands.description:

work has reached the integration branch: a plan branch once
its plan is there, a build once its verification passes there,
a slicing or sandbox once every cycle it carries is, anything
of an abandoned cycle, and anything of a cycle the harvest
ledger there records closed. Prints the removal for a person to run.
Deletes nothing, and leaves remote branches alone.

commands.name: unpark
commands.description:

with a passing verify; its spec and plan are then read again
against what merged. Refuses one still waiting, saying why.

commands.name: upgrade
commands.description:

each is on now: this machine's tool, the plugin, this
solution's pin and what 'sdlc init' writes, the factory's
images when it has one, and the open cycles still pinning an
older release. Without a release, the one this machine runs.
Always answered by this machine's release, never the pinned
one. Runs nothing.

it does not hold. This is the pull-request check. --base is the
target branch: a pull request changing only the cycle's
planning documents then gets the admission check -- plan,
approval, hashes, no verify.
verify-chain slices/<slug>/plan --base <branch>

carries gets the admission check, its successors must be
sound, and a plan that needs a file only a sibling's plan
creates is refused (D-125).
verify-chain <branch> --base <branch>

it changes is the pin, what 'sdlc init' and 'sdlc factory'
write, answers in the declared stack to what the release asks,
and dependency versions. Each file must be what this release
writes from the base's copy, a pipeline step by step (D-133);
a dependency file may move only versions, of any size (D-134).
Anything else is refused: there is no chain.
admission <id> --base <branch>
Print true when a pull request carries only the cycle's
planning documents, and any successors, so a pipeline may
skip the build and tests; false for anything else. On
slices/<slug>/plan, true when it carries only cycles'
planning and successors. Always exits 0.
promotion <source> --base <target>
Print true when a pull request promotes the integration
branch or a release/* branch into another branch, so a
pipeline skips the chain; false when it targets the
integration branch or a release branch. Exits 1 when any
other branch targets another branch.

commands.description:

expects beside it. Inside a solution that pins another
release, every command -- this one too -- is answered by
the pinned release. With SDLC_DEV_BUILD set, by that build,
which calls itself <release>-local.

did. A row not true here says 'none' rather than being

count on Azure DevOps, and on GitHub, which never counts
it, needs a team: --self-approve <team> lets that team
bypass the rules on a pull request.
branch <id> <kind>      Print the one git command that puts the working copy on the
branch a kind of work happens on -- plan, build,
build-unattended or forward -- creating it from the right
base: the integration branch once the plan is admitted to
it, before that the plan's own branch or the admission
branch carrying it. A plan only in a sandbox is refused
until 'sdlc admit' takes it out. 'sandbox' opens a
worktree on sandbox/<id> beside the repository, where every
cycle the work turns into is planned. 'plan --worktree'
opens the one cycle in a folder of its own. 'plan' without a
worktree refuses uncommitted work, which the switch would
carry, and a local plan branch whose ledger lacks the
approval the integration branch holds (D-123).

the local branch or the remote's. Where remediation works, on
a blocked, escalated or passed cycle (D-185).

placed in the sandbox if it is uncommitted, admits the plan
when it is only in a sandbox, opens the build's worktree beside
the repository, starts the build's own process there running

options.name: /sdlc
options.description:
never with permission checks off, never marked as a reader --
waits, and prints the report. Exits 0 on a pass, 1 on blocked
or escalated. With no id, every queued cycle in one process
started from here, each in a worktree of its own; a plan only
in a sandbox is queued only when named. Refuses when the
build's process cannot start, or ends without a report. The

commands.description:
